request.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural / composition refinement.
Create ONE refined FOUR-photo contact sheet for the Vegetable Guides section opener of The Vegetable Guru. Develop only photographs numbered 2, 3, 4 and 5 in reference image 1, responding carefully to the user's composition feedback. Do not include former images 1 or 6. These four are promising directions, not final selections.

REFERENCE ROLES:
1: previous six-image contact sheet, the EDIT TARGET and source of the four compositions to develop. Keep the recognisable subjects and natural photographic character, but change composition as specified below. Do not reproduce all six or the same grid.
2: A43, actual camera photograph of the real leek bed: use for true plant density, varied leaf anatomy, soil and bed perspective in new photo 3.
3: LOOKDOWN, actual downward-profile reference sheet for John's face. Use only the real photographic panels to preserve the lowered face; do not copy winter clothes, cap or the illustrated tile. Short grey beard follows jaw back towards throat, lower lip ahead of chin, never a projecting rounded beard.
4: J02, real John for mature build, identity, receding grey hair and olive summer T-shirt/shorts; same clothes in new photo 5, bareheaded. Do not copy this reference's presenting gesture or camera eye contact.
5: H31, actual home garden setting, path and soil-bed relationship for photo 5 and true courgette plant character for photo 2. Keep real small-garden scale and materials; choose a crop/camera position that hides competing garden fixtures.

SHEET FORMAT:
FOUR equal portrait photos in TWO columns and TWO rows on a narrow off-white sheet. Overall sheet portrait approximately 1070 pixels WIDE × 1450 pixels HIGH. Each photo roughly 520 wide × 675 high, matching 185:240 book page proportions. NOT square panels or phone-shaped panels. Narrow off-white gutters. A small clear black numeral outside and BELOW each photograph: top left "2", top right "3", bottom left "4", bottom right "5". Keep these original numbers for comparison. These four numerals are the ONLY text. No page titles, captions, designs or contents lists.

THE COMPOSITION RULE:
One immediately clear subject in each photograph. The viewer should instantly see courgettes, leeks, flowering beans, or John absorbed in gardening. This must come from camera position, framing, natural visual hierarchy and plausible optical depth of field. Avoid busy unrelated structures, competing props and random decorative additions. Preserve realistic gardening, seasonal plants and candid activity. These are observed living plants, not still-life arrangements.

TOP LEFT — 2 / COURGETTES:
A closer, cleaner development of former photo 2. Make the attached dark-green courgettes the unmistakable subject: one handsome but ordinary-sized fruit prominent in lower-middle frame, and perhaps a second smaller fruit behind it, both growing naturally from the plant crown with correct stems and a yellow blossom. Fruits sit above/beside the soil as real courgettes do, not lying loose. Frame surrounding broad courgette leaves as a natural cradle rather than a wall concealing the fruit. Replace the distracting climbing beans behind with softly receding foliage belonging to the SAME courgette plant/bed. NO beans, trellis, greenhouse, pots or garden vista. Recognisable leaf lobes and modest natural silvery markings, not a flat decorative pattern. Bright soft daylight on fruit and flower, subtle shade behind. No giant marrow, supermarket polish or staged dew. Plenty of leaf texture but one visual centre.

TOP RIGHT — 3 / LEEKS:
Develop the strong repeating rhythm of former photo 3, moving the camera closer and slightly downward. A few uneven, healthy blue-green leek plants lead from the foreground into a softly receding row; credible slightly different thicknesses, heights and lean, white-to-green lower shafts entering actual soil. Keep the plants and soil in focus across a useful foreground depth and let the farther leek leaves blur gently. Crop OUT sky, trees, houses, shed, water butt and visible garden clutter. A tiny edge of the existing path may appear only if subordinate; otherwise fill the portrait entirely with this coherent leek-bed world. Natural spacing with soil gaps, occasional bent/tipped leaves. No artificial perfectly repeated fans or manicured wall of greenery. The actual A43 camera reference controls botanical character.

BOTTOM LEFT — 4 / FLOWERING CLIMBING BEANS:
Keep the successful oblique arrangement of former photo 4: a foreground vine and slender bamboo, a few hanging bean pods and a receding row. Give it life with authentic SCARLET RUNNER-BEAN FLOWERS attached naturally on small flower racemes among the heart-shaped runner-bean leaves. Several modest red flower clusters at varying stages and depths, with a few buds; enough colour to enliven the green photograph, not huge red bouquets or flowers pasted on top. Runner pods and leaves must be anatomically consistent with runner beans. Preserve natural asymmetry and some open pockets. Bamboo slender, weathered and tapered with small nodes/green wire tie, not thick poles. Background is soft bean foliage and soil only; remove the competing shed and recognisable buildings through framing and optical depth of field. Flowers belong to the crop itself, not unrelated ornamental plants.

BOTTOM RIGHT — 5 / JOHN TENDING THE BED:
Keep the natural crouched action from former photo 5 but move the camera a little farther away: John about 25–30% smaller in the frame, with comfortable space around his body. His torso/head/hands must remain the one clear focal subject. He is unaware of camera, looking down as he gently parts a courgette leaf while tending the plant; one hand rests on his knee, the other works naturally. Olive T-shirt and shorts, real mature proportions, short greying beard and receding hair. Use the real profile from reference 3 for the downward face and reference 4 for body/outfit. Frame through a restrained layer of foreground leaves that leads toward him. His feet are on the actual slab path beside the soil bed. Pick a tighter garden direction/lower angle so the herb trough, pots, greenhouse and unrelated structures are hidden behind foliage or excluded; do NOT bring back the scattered subjects of former photo 1. Background soft hedge/bed foliage, with believable optical separation. No looking up, camera smile, produce presenting or staged tool. Body should remain comfortably within the photograph and feel like a real person in his own working garden.

SHARED FINISH:
Beautiful but honest photographic detail, natural UK summer light, restrained greens and the real yellow courgette flower/red runner-bean flower accents. Moderate natural depth of field, not smeared cutout blur. Varied leaf sizes and wear, a few tiny imperfections, soil gaps. No staged harvest, fancy props, perfect repeated plants, synthetic shine, cinematic grading, painted style or artificial vignette. Photographic realism throughout.
Future white page titles will be laid out separately. Where possible, allow quieter upper foliage without sacrificing the composition, but do not add any white title now. The bottom strip remains expendable for possible contents. Main subjects kept clear of trim. This sheet is for comparing four stronger SUBJECT-LED COMPOSITIONS, not final print production.
